specifically at Miss mixed use properties.

There are two items outlined in the contract that have financial implications, including the total contract costs and the addition of a termination clause and the impacts of that clause for both parties.
The first financial item, as I mentioned, is the total contract cost.
Several financial assumptions were made during the original negotiations with Cosmopolitan Industries back in 2013 and 2014 that have not come to fruition and have had impacts on Cosmos operations.
These relate primarily to a decrease in the value of commodities and the limited market options for selling recycling for cycles.
As a result, the contract renewal includes a baseline adjustment of 19% in the first year followed by a 3% increase thereafter.

In comparison to the recently renewed Curbside Recycling Contract for single-family properties, in that case the city agreed to a 30% increase in the first year followed by a 2% increase annually to compensate for
the changes in recycling markets.
The cost of this contract is funded by a recycling utility fee for multi-unit properties involved in the program and is also subsidized through the multi-material stewardship western or MMSW program.
Assuming the same proportions going forward from a subsidy and a utility rate perspective, the utility rate is estimated to increase by 24 cents a month in 2024.
The second item is related to the unknown impacts of the province's new extended producer program.
In order to protect both parties, the contract includes a clause in the event that the contract needs to be terminated before expiration.
Cosmopolitan will be making a capital investment for some of their equipment to be able to continue to deliver recycling services for the next six years.
And from the city's perspective, there is currently no early termination provision in the contract.
Therefore, what is included is a pro-rated capital cost recovery clause in the event that the contract needs to be terminated as well as 75% payment of net profits.
Both of these are considered worst case scenarios and based on what we have seen in other provinces that are further along in their extended producer responsibility programs.
We do not anticipate having to enact these clauses, but they are there in the event that either party needs to enact them.

The recommendation in the report is for council to approve the six year renewal and the proposed contract amendments for the multi-unit residential recycling program with cause and policy industries, which is set to expire at the end of this year.
